# Requesty

Router across many providers with fallbacks and spend limits.

| | |
|---|---|
| Kind | Chat API (OpenAI-compatible): returns code that conductor applies |
| Cost | Paid, per token |
| Key | `REQUESTY_API_KEY` from https://app.requesty.ai/api-keys |
| Endpoint | `https://router.requesty.ai/v1` |
| Default model | picked automatically from the live list (coding models first); choose your own with `conductor models requesty --all` |
| conductor name | `requesty` |
| Provider docs | https://docs.requesty.ai/quickstart |
| Checked | 2026-11 |

## Set up

1. Create an API key: https://app.requesty.ai/api-keys
2. Add it to conductor. It asks for the key (hidden input), lets you pick a model, sends one test prompt and adds it to the `docs`, `test`, `review` and `ask` roles:
   ```bash
   conductor add requesty
   ```
3. Check it any time:
   ```bash
   conductor doctor --live
   ```

Or click **Add** on its card in `conductor ui` → Providers.

## Without the wizard

Save the key (hidden input; or pipe it in):
```bash
conductor keys set REQUESTY_API_KEY
```

Then add this to `~/.config/conductor/config.json` (all projects) or `.conductor/config.json` (one project):
```json
{
  "providers": {
    "requesty": {
      "type": "openai",
      "enabled": true,
      "baseUrl": "https://router.requesty.ai/v1",
      "apiKeyEnv": "REQUESTY_API_KEY",
      "model": "<model id>"
    }
  }
}
```
List models: `conductor models requesty --all`. Put `requesty` in any role's chain in `conductor ui` → Roles & fallback.

The variable name only tells conductor where to find the key; the provider never sees it. To use a key you already keep under another name, set `"apiKeyEnv": "YOUR_VAR"` on `requesty`.

## Troubleshooting

- **401 / 403**: the key is wrong, expired, or still a placeholder. Run `conductor keys` to see where it comes from, then `conductor keys set REQUESTY_API_KEY`.
- **404 or "model not found"**: the model id changed. Pick a current one with `conductor models requesty --all`.
- **429**: rate limit. conductor puts the provider on cooldown and moves to the next one in the chain; `conductor cooldown --clear requesty` resets it.
- **Empty reply**: some free routes return nothing now and then; conductor retries once, then falls back.
